CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys in a child with Smith-Magenis syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old female (soon to be 2 years old) who presents for evaluation of her kidneys. She is a former 34 and 3-week gestation twin, born weighing 4 pounds 8 ounces, with her twin sister weighing 3 pounds 13 ounces. She was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis syndrome by neurology after presenting with significant developmental delay. She was not sitting independently by 12 months of age but is now crawling and attempting to take steps. As an infant, she had apneic episodes with feeding (preemie-type issues) and difficulty regulating temperature. She has severe gastroesophageal reflux managed by GI. She is intolerant to cow's milk and has been switched to ripple pea protein milk with improved fluid intake. She currently produces approximately 8-10 wet diapers per 24 hours. The geneticist informed the family that Smith-Magenis syndrome may be associated with kidney abnormalities, including potential kidney fusion, prompting this referral.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Respiratory: History of apneic episodes with feeding as infant.
Gastrointestinal: Severe reflux; cow's milk intolerance.
Genitourinary: Normal wet diaper frequency.
Neurological: Developmental delay with hypotonia; improved motor function with crawling and weight-bearing attempts.
Other: Patient has been evaluated by multiple specialists including neurology, GI, allergy, dietetics, feeding therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, orthopedics, ophthalmology, and audiology.

Lives in Dallas, Georgia. Has older brother (age 9 years) with autism and an identical twin sister who is healthy and developmentally normal. Twin sister is running and playing appropriately. Twins are approximately the same size and wear the same clothing, though the twin sister is slightly taller. Patient is slightly shorter in stature.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-nourished female, slightly fussy when examined.
HEENT: Eyes small appearing.
Neurological: Mild hypotonia of the lower extremities and arms.
Cardiovascular: Heart examined.
Pulmonary: Lungs examined.
Ears: Examined.
Genitalia: Normal external female genitalia.

RESULTS
No imaging results available at this time. Kidney ultrasound ordered and pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3-week gestation twin with Smith-Magenis syndrome, a chromosomal deletion syndrome that can affect multiple organ systems. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in association with this syndrome.

1. Obtain kidney ultrasound screening today to evaluate for congenital renal abnormalities.
2. If ultrasound is normal, no further nephrology follow-up is needed.
3. If ultrasound shows abnormalities, will determine next steps and arrange appropriate follow-up at the Kennesaw location.
4. Nurse will provide ultrasound instructions and complete paperwork prior to discharge.
5. Physician will call patient with results.
